rv: The (before unknown) connecttions between Chicken and fabric

After going on about how textiles (that's pronounced Tex-tills people!) is used in our everyday lives, we are treated to an EXCELLENT overview of how thread and fabric are made, from cotton piles to the finished product. This is one of the more entertaining 'assembly line' sequences I have ever seen. After that, it suddenly veers off into an unexpected territory about the benefits the textile factory brings to the town. Schools! Dances! Barbecue Chicken!…

This early '50s film produced by the textile industry is a paean to an industry that doesn't exist in this country anymore. There a few pro forma references to unspecified "mistakes of the past" (brutal child labor? savage union-busting? totalitarian company towns?), but, hey, that was then!
